routes.description: Infer God from causal dependence, natural order, objective moral obligation, and the explanatory reach of Thomistic natural theology.
routes.successCriteria: Establish that dependent causal series require a purely actual source, that objective morality requires a divine intellect, and that natural effects can support extranatural explanation.

motionBridge.description: The convergent causal, moral, and natural-theology inferences must warrant identifying their ultimate explanation as God.

centralBridges.description: Change and instrumental causal dependence must terminate in a purely actual first source rather than an infinite series of potencies.
Objective moral wrongness must exist independently of human opinion and require grounding in a divine intellect.
Natural observations must legitimately support inference to a supernatural creator, necessary being, or intelligent designer.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Stable lawlike behavior by mindless natural objects must support an ordering intelligence behind natural regularities.
Thomistic proofs must share a defensible inference-to-best-explanation structure with scientific reasoning.

routes.description: Require supported demonstrations for God, challenge the transition from natural phenomena to divine attributes, and supply non-theistic accounts of morality and scientific explanation.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the affirmative inferences do not establish a divine mind, that supernatural explanations remain undemonstrated, and that moral assessment does not require divine law.

motionBridge.description: The God claim must remain unwarranted unless its definition, existence, and claimed attributes are established by valid argument and sufficient evidence.

centralBridges.description: Observed causal relations must not be extended beyond accessible cosmic history or identified with an atemporal divine mind without support.
Explanatory inference must not admit supernatural candidates unless their existence and explanatory relevance are demonstrable.
Moral consequences must remain objectively assessable relative to human well-being without requiring an independently existing divine moral law.

subsidiaryBridges.description: A capable God who wants belief must be expected to provide verifiable and sufficient evidence of his existence.
Finite observers must have a method for distinguishing a powerful cause from the creator, sustainer, and moral foundation of classical theism.

sections.title: Causal Dependence and a First Source
sections.rationale: This issue tests the principal Thomistic inference from observed change and dependent causal series to a purely actual source identified as God.

sections.title: Evidence, Divine Attributes, and Hiddenness
sections.rationale: This issue determines what evidence the God claim requires and whether natural order or alleged disclosure connects the proposed explanation to classical theism.

sections.title: Science and Supernatural Explanation
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether scientific inference permits supernatural causes and whether Thomistic arguments possess the claimed explanatory structure.

sections.title: Objective Morality and Divine Grounding
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether objective moral judgments require a divine intellect or can instead be assessed through non-theistic foundations and physical consequences.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Aquinas's arguments from change, causation, and contingency require an actual and necessary source beyond dependent natural chains, identified as God.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: The reliable goal-directed behavior of mindless natural objects implies that an intelligent mind guides natural laws and regularities.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Objective moral obligations exist beyond individual opinion and therefore require a divine intellect in which moral law is grounded.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Theism bears the burden of proof, and an undefined or unfalsifiable God claim cannot reasonably be accepted merely because atheists cannot conclusively disprove it.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: A God who wants belief and can provide detectable evidence should successfully reveal himself, yet alleged revelations remain unverifiable or insufficient and Dillahunty remains unconvinced.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c05.proposition: Causal regularities observed within the universe cannot simply be extended beyond its accessible history, and existence outside time is not a demonstrated or coherent premise.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c07.proposition: Change proceeds from potency to actuality through an instrumental causal series that cannot regress infinitely and therefore requires a purely actual first mover identified as God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c08.proposition: Even if a model suggests a first cause, it neither establishes that the cause is God or a mind nor explains coherent atemporal causation, while laws of nature are descriptions rather than products requiring a lawgiver.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c10.proposition: Explanatory inference cannot admit undemonstrated supernatural candidates, and ignorance about cosmic origins does not make a supernatural cause plausible or true.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c02.proposition: Science can infer supernatural causes from natural effects because singularities themselves lie outside nature while remaining scientifically invoked.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c03.proposition: Methodological naturalism permits science to use only demonstrable natural explanations, not undetectable supernatural entities or causes.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c05.proposition: Aquinas's Five Ways qualify as scientific inductive arguments because they organize observations in nature into inferences to the best explanation.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c07.proposition: The existence of objectively wrong acts independent of human opinion points to an objective moral law and therefore to a divine intellect.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c08.proposition: Once morality is grounded in the well-being of thinking creatures, objective physical facts permit assessments without a universal divine moral law.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-03.proposition: Objective moral laws have not been demonstrated to exist as independent entities, and belief in such a code neither identifies its content nor establishes that the believer's preferred values are correct.
